entities.name: Cynan ab Iago
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Cynan ab Iago (died 1063-10-14) was a pivotal, though often overshadowed, Welsh prince of the House of Aberffraw, whose primary historical significance derives from his father, Iago ab Idwal ap Meurig, King of Gwynedd, and his son, Gruffudd ap Cynan, who would later become a monumental figure in Welsh resistance against Anglo-Norman encroachment. Born into the tumultuous dynastic struggles of 11th-century Wales, Cynan's life was shaped by exile and a strategic marriage, ultimately ensuring the continuation of a royal lineage that would profoundly impact the political landscape of medieval Wales for generations.

Following the deposition and likely death of his father, Iago ab Idwal, King of Gwynedd, in 1039, Cynan was forced into exile, seeking refuge in Dublin, then a prominent Viking-Norse kingdom. During his exile, he forged a crucial alliance through marriage to Ragnhild, daughter of Olaf Sigtryggsson, King of Dublin. This union was instrumental, as it provided his son, Gruffudd, with powerful maternal connections to the Norse-Gaelic elite of Ireland and the Irish Sea region, a resource Gruffudd would later exploit for military support in his relentless campaigns to reclaim his ancestral kingdom. Cynan himself made at least one documented attempt to return to Wales and assert his claim to Gwynedd, though this effort ultimately proved unsuccessful, leaving the task of restoration to his formidable son.
